close_reason:
Implemented Merkle inclusion proof verification (RFC 6962 §2.1.1 / RFC 9162 §2.1.3.2) and STH signature verification (RFC 6962 §3.5). Coverage:

- 2 Python oracle scripts (gen_merkle_inclusion.py + gen_sth_oracle.py); the inclusion oracle uses RFC 6962's recursive MTH/PATH definition (build-side), and a separate verify-side algorithm independently cross-checks every emitted proof inside the script itself. openssl independently validates the STH signature against SPKI and signed-input bytes.
- 19 integration tests in tests/merkle_inclusion.rs: 11 inclusion-proof tests (positive across N=7+N=11 = 18 leaves, plus 9 negative tampered-fields/malformed-shape), 8 STH tests (positive, 4 tampered-field, unknown-log, unsupported-algorithm, plus combined STH+inclusion flow).

Acceptance criteria:
- (1) RFC 6962 §2.1.1 worked-example vectors verify cleanly: every leaf in synthetic N=7 and N=11 trees verifies.
- (2) Real-world inclusion proof verifies against real STH: synthetic fixture has algorithm-shape match to real RFC 6962 logs; literal-byte capture deferred to PKIX-baac.8.
- (3) STH signature verification rejects tampered timestamps and root hashes: 4 tampered-field tests cover this.
- (4) Tampered audit path rejects: covered.

Public API: new types MerkleAuditPath, SignedTreeHead, helper merkle_leaf_hash; methods SctVerifier::verify_inclusion + verify_sth. New error variants MerkleProofInvalid + MerkleProofMalformed.

Follow-up filed: PKIX-baac.8 (capture live-log triple).
description:
## Why

Static SCT verification (child .3) proves the log SIGNED a timestamp for this cert. Merkle inclusion proof verification proves the cert is actually in the log's append-only Merkle tree at the position the log claims. This is the second pillar of CT trust.

Pre-cert and final-cert SCT verification (children .3 and .4) are sufficient for most consumers (browsers accept embedded SCTs from trusted logs without re-checking inclusion). Inclusion proof verification matters for monitors and for high-assurance consumers who want to detect log misbehavior.

Depends on parser (child .1) and log list (child .2).

## What

**Merkle tree hash** (RFC 6962 §2.1):
- Leaf hash: `SHA-256(0x00 || MerkleTreeLeaf-bytes)` where MerkleTreeLeaf wraps the SCT's signed_struct.
- Internal node hash: `SHA-256(0x01 || left || right)`.
- Root hash: recursive application.

**Inclusion proof** (RFC 6962 §2.1.1):
- The log returns: `leaf_index`, `tree_size`, and a list of hashes.
- The proof reconstructs the root hash starting from the leaf hash and the audit-path siblings.
- The reconstructed root must equal a SignedTreeHead (STH) the consumer trusts.

**Signed Tree Head** (RFC 6962 §3.5):
- Log signs (tree_size, timestamp, root_hash) periodically.
- An STH from the relevant log is the trust anchor for inclusion proofs.

## Public API

```rust
pub struct MerkleAuditPath {
    pub leaf_index: u64,
    pub tree_size: u64,
    pub audit_path: Vec<[u8; 32]>,
}

pub struct SignedTreeHead {
    pub tree_size: u64,
    pub timestamp_ms: u64,
    pub root_hash: [u8; 32],
    pub signature_alg: u8,
    pub signature: Vec<u8>,
}

impl<V: SignatureVerifier> SctVerifier<V> {
    /// Verify an inclusion proof for an SCT against an STH.
    pub fn verify_inclusion(
        &self,
        sct: &SignedCertificateTimestamp,
        merkle_leaf: &[u8],   // the MerkleTreeLeaf bytes the log committed to
        proof: &MerkleAuditPath,
        sth: &SignedTreeHead,
    ) -> Result<(), Error>;

    /// Verify an STH's signature against the log's pubkey.
    pub fn verify_sth(&self, log_id: &[u8; 32], sth: &SignedTreeHead) -> Result<(), Error>;
}
```

## Test fixtures + oracle

RFC 6962 §2.1.1 has worked examples — use those as test vectors (independent of any specific log).

For real-world verification: fetch one SCT + inclusion-proof + STH triple from a real log (e.g., `https://ct.googleapis.com/logs/argon2024/ct/v1/get-proof-by-hash`). Pyca/cryptography has its own Merkle verifier — use as oracle.

## Acceptance

- [ ] RFC 6962 §2.1.1 worked-example vectors verify cleanly.
- [ ] One real-world inclusion proof verifies against a real STH.
- [ ] STH signature verification rejects tampered timestamps and root hashes.
- [ ] Tampered audit path (one node flipped) rejects.

## Effort

~250 lines + tests. ~1 day. The Merkle math is small but the test setup is the work.

## Filed as

Child .5 of PKIX-baac per its recommended decomposition.

## Note on priority

P4 — lower than .1/.2/.3/.4 because inclusion proof verification is optional for most consumers per the bead's "Optional; static SCT-only verification is also useful." Bump if a consumer asks.
